title: VDBE operation-array growth and fixed-operand append core

scope.rationale: These eight mutually coupled vdbeaux.c routines implement the smallest operation-array append state machine: geometric growth, allocator-reported capacity, fixed P1/P2/P3 initialization, and P4_INT32 insertion.
excluded_responsibilities: VDBE object creation and linked-list ownership
operation-list transfer, readiness, execution, reset, and deletion

dependencies.caller_closure: Compiler callers remain inventoried separately. This unit cannot pass admission until its exact representation and connection-allocation dependencies have atomic dossiers at source-translated or later.

inputs: An INIT-state Vdbe with its owning Parse and sqlite3 connection
A canonical u8 opcode and fixed integer operands
outputs: An allocator-sized Vdbe.aOp array with initialized opcode, P1-P5, and P4 type/value
contracts.ownership: The connection allocator owns aOp. Reallocation preserves the old pointer and capacity on failure; successful growth updates Parse.szOpAlloc from allocator usable size.
contracts.state_and_results: nOp advances only after capacity exists. Growth limit or allocation failure sets connection OOM state and the slow append returns SQLite's historical sentinel address 1.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: Caller holds the connection mutex. No callbacks or I/O occur.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: On OOM, existing operations remain owned and destructible; callers observe sticky sqlite3.mallocFailed and stop meaningful code generation.

representation_differences: The C integer opcode parameter is a generated Zig enum(u8), making the source range assertion structural.
The Parse.db pointer is opaque in the cycle-breaking Parse layout module and is converted back to the exact sqlite3 type at the vdbeaux boundary.
The active profile omits test realloc stress, explain comments, statement scan status, VDBE profiling, debug add-op tracing, and VDBE coverage fields; only selected branches are translated.

oracle.protocol: One neutral symbolic sequence names AddOp0/AddOp1/AddOp2/AddOp3/AddOp4Int operations, successful geometric growth, limit OOM, reached one-shot and sticky allocation failures, sticky persistence, and post-clear continuation; C and Zig adapters emit addresses, capacities, operands, P4 types, mallocFailed, and ownership state. The comparator also mutates an emitted capacity and proves the divergence is rejected.
internal_observations: append address and nOp before/after each operation
growth-limit and reached one-shot realloc failure
old-array identity and contents after failure
oracle.normalization: Pointer addresses are replaced only by stable allocation identities; capacities, operation bytes, results, and event order are exact.

assurance.oom: Native and differential traces cover initial growth-limit OOM, reached one-shot and sticky growth allocation failures, sticky persistence across machine reset, preservation of the existing operation array, and continuation after explicit fault/OOM clear.
assurance.io_crash_concurrency: No I/O; connection mutex is a caller obligation.
assurance.malformed_input: Internal trusted API with source assertions; invalid opcodes are unrepresentable in Zig.
assurance.continuation: Oracle traces prove the old array and operation count remain intact after growth failure and appends resume after OOM clear.
assurance.performance: Geometric growth and allocator-sized capacity are preserved; no benchmark credit yet.

integration.bounded_owner_retired: No. Program construction in src/core/vdbe.zig and sql_frontend.zig remains frozen pending the complete builder/compiler ownership switch.

The source-corresponding builder is not yet the production compiler owner; handwritten Program construction must be retired before integration.
